newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil rebels seize N.Korean ship, one crew killed.
newsitem.headline: Tamil rebels seize N.Korean ship, one crew killed.

text.p: Tamil Tiger separatists said on Tuesday they had seized a North Korean merchant ship off northern Sri Lanka and one of its 38 crew members was killed in a shootout when he tried to escape.

Clandestine Voice of Tiger radio, monitored in government-controlled territory, said Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) rebels boarded the ship Morang Bong on Monday night and took it to a northeastern coastal base.
Tiger radio said the rebels were making arrangements to release the remaining crew. It did not give further details.

A Defence Ministry statement said on Tuesday the North Korean ship was captured by the LTTE while some eight km (five miles) off Point Pedro on the former northern rebel stronghold of Jaffna peninsula.
It said the ship was now anchored off Challai on the northeastern coast of Sri Lanka, which is under rebel control.

"This ship had been chartered by traders from Colombo to carry essential goods to Point Pedro for the civilians in the north. This was the second trip of this vessel to the north," the statement said.

An official of Monsell International, the ship's agent in Colombo, earlier told Reuters that the ship had carried nearly 3,000 tonnes of food and essential items to Point Pedro and was hijacked after it had unloaded its cargo.
"The ship, Morang Bong, is registered in North Korea and had 38 North Korean crew," the official said.
Food and other essential supplies are taken to Jaffna by air or sea as there is no land route connecting the peninsula with the rest of the island.

Some 20,000 Sri Lankan troops are battling LTTE fighters to open a highway through the northern rebel-held Wanni region toward Jaffna. But a government offensive launched in May has slowed down following fierce counterattacks by the rebels.
Tamil rebels set fire to a refugee ship off the northwestern coast last week and took away its nine crew, including two Indonesians. They were freed later and the ship was destroyed.

The LTTE has been fighting since 1983 for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in Sri Lanka's north and east. The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed in the war while the LTTE puts the toll higher.
